Q1_one_read_provides_complete_validated_.method: handle.read(0, undefined) on an official read handle

Q2_closers_apply_directly_to_those_event.method: interruptedTurnClosers(storedEvents) over the SAME array the read returned

Q3_reproduces_official_cold_read_recover.method: byte-level comparison of seq/type/reason between the single-read derivation and readColdSessionLog

Q4_ownership_of_returned_event_graph.method: read the SessionSeedEventState the handle reports
Q4_ownership_of_returned_event_graph.note: the OUTER array returned by read is caller-owned; the event VALUES are shared-frozen, so the adapter must treat them as immutable and never write through them

Q5_recovery_helper_input_mutation.method: compare the input array length before and after interruptedTurnClosers

Q9_header_paired_with_the_same_read_hand.method: compare handle.header/handle.inheritedEventCount with the official ColdSessionLog header fields

Q10_inherited_events_and_fork_lineage_wi.method: read handle.inheritedEventCount and the header lineage fields from the SAME handle

Q6_one_read_invocation_yields_a_consiste.method: one handle.read call resolves one physical generation and returns a slice of it
Q6_one_read_invocation_yields_a_consiste.sourceNote: JsonlSessionHandle.read -> readCurrent -> resolveCurrentLog once, then readStoredLog once; a monotonic observedLength guard rejects a shrunken log

Q7_ordering_and_snapshot_guarantees_for_.method: append+flush a writer between two reads on one read handle
Q7_ordering_and_snapshot_guarantees_for_.documentedContract: SessionHandle: 'Reads concurrent with a mutation carry no ordering promise beyond the valid contiguous prefix'; 'a torn physical tail is never returned'; 'repeated reads on this handle never observe an older state than a prior read'
Q7_ordering_and_snapshot_guarantees_for_.verdict: ONE_READ_IS_A_VALID_CONTIGUOUS_PREFIX; the boundary of an already-observed read is never retroactively reclassified

observed.append: on resolution the batch is accepted, ordered, and visible to reads on this backend instance; a backend may buffer or batch physical writes behind append
observed.flush: the durability barrier — on resolution every acknowledged append is durable and the session is materialized for other processes

Q8_append_flush_and_crash_durability.evidentiaryMeaningOfPersistedDshEvent: an event READ BACK from this persistence backend's stored log; it does NOT by itself prove a resolved flush barrier, crash durability, Work settlement, tool success, promotion or a verified Attempt→Session binding

Q11_errors_that_must_remain_distinguisha.method: trigger each failure against the installed backend and record the error NAME

readOnlyAppend.name: SessionReadOnlyError
readOnlyAppend.message: session "audit-balanced": append is not available on a read handle

readAfterClose.name: SessionHandleClosedError
readAfterClose.message: session "audit-balanced": read on a closed handle

Q12_closing_after_a_successful_read.method: close twice on a read handle whose read already succeeded
Q12_closing_after_a_successful_read.contract: close() is idempotent and uncancellable: `this.closing ??= (async () => ...)`, so a second call observes the first settlement
Q12_closing_after_a_successful_read.verdict: CLOSE_IS_IDEMPOTENT; a close failure must be surfaced separately and must never discard or fabricate the read result

Q13_installed_api_behaves_as_expected_un.method: every probe above ran on this Node version
Q13_installed_api_behaves_as_expected_un.verdict: BEHAVES_AS_DOCUMENTED; the Node version is BELOW the repository's declared minimum and is recorded as an environment caveat
